children: Industrials have delivered solid gains in 2026, but the sector has recently given back some ground as higher borrowing costs, elevated oil prices and renewed concerns around manufacturing activity have weighed on sentiment.
The S&P 500 Industrials sector was up 9.8% year to date, compared with a 12.6% gain for the broader S&P 500, while the sector was down 5.4% over the past month.

The sector's performance has been supported by areas such as aerospace and defense and the broader investment cycle, although U.S. factory output unexpectedly fell 0.3% in August after seven consecutive monthly gains, highlighting pressure from rising costs and softer manufacturing momentum.
Against this backdrop, a quantitative screen identifies nine industrials-sector stocks that have maintained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for at least 60 consecutive days.

The group spans industrial machinery and supplies, data processing and outsourced services, trading companies and distributors, building products, construction and engineering, electrical components and equipment, and industrial conglomerates.
leads the list, having maintained a Sell or Strong Sell Quant Rating for 200 consecutive days. Verra Mobility Corporation
follows with 136 consecutive days, while SiteOne Landscape Supply, Inc.
have maintained the ratings for 113 and 112 days, respectively. Primoris Services Corporation
rounds out the top five with 102 consecutive days.
The screen also includes ESAB Corporation
. Honeywell is the largest company among the listed names, with a market capitalization of approximately $67.4 billion, providing exposure to a broad range of industrial businesses.

The companies span several areas of the industrial economy, from machinery and building products to construction, electrical equipment and industrial technology. Their inclusion in the screen reflects sustained weakness across the quantitative factors used by Seeking Alpha rather than a single industry-specific trend.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers.
